verdict: FireHydrant: Choose FireHydrant when incident command with a published $25 Pro floor is the job — not PagerDuty by default, and not Datadog/Honeycomb. Scores use the IT & Development editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing.
weaknesses: Paging is not the lead SKU
bestFor: Teams that want incident command with a 10-responder free path
Buyers comparing FireHydrant Pro $25 to Rootly $20 and incident.io Team $15
Orgs that will keep PagerDuty for paging and add FireHydrant for command
notIdealFor: Orgs whose primary job is PagerDuty-style on-call paging at enterprise scale
ITSM ticket desks without incident command
tradeoffs: Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models
Module stacking and consumption overages vs single-SKU floors
Free tiers vs enterprise SSO/audit gates
Landscape-adjacent tools vs primary job-cluster peers on best pages
recommendation: Choose FireHydrant when incident command with a published $25 Pro floor is the job — not PagerDuty by default, and not Datadog/Honeycomb. Compare PagerDuty for paging-first on-call; incident.io or Rootly for other product-led incident SKUs.
editorialNotes: IT Tier-B + ITSM SMB batch. Approved on it-development-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=incident-oncall. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the eight IT editorial criteria using category weights (IT job fit 16, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, admin/security 12, value 12, AI 12, scalability 10), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ITSM, observability, source control, hosting panels, and web-data platforms are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
